tools.name: verify_connection
tools.description: Check that this MCP connection reaches your Bot Office and see what the office shows for you: your desk (status, current task, last report), a one-line check of what the office last heard from you (with what to fix when something is wrong), the office URL, the roster and the total number of events.

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: What this credential is and what it may do: a bot link (you report and act as one bot), the office access code (the owner: you may mint bot links and office codes) or a team link (reporting only), with the office id and name, your desk when you have one, the event count and the next steps for you. tools.name: list_office_agents
tools.description: List the agents in your Bot Office (id, name, status, role) so you can pick the right to_agent_id for a handoff or an escalation.

tools.name: perform_action
tools.description: Do something in a system the owner connected (ServiceNow, Remedy, Jira, Zendesk, Zabbix, PagerDuty, Slack, AWS, vSphere, GitHub, Twilio, Salesforce, HubSpot, Shopify, Stripe): create or update a ticket, acknowledge an alert, start or reboot an instance, move a deal, send a text, refund an order. tools.name: list_actions
tools.description: The actions you may perform right now: the catalog filtered to your role's allowed kinds and to the systems this workspace has connections for, with each action's risk tier (0 read … 4 destructive), params and whether it supports a dry run. tools.name: check_action
tools.description: The current status of an action you requested (awaiting_approval, approved, running, succeeded, failed, rejected, expired), with its result or error and its audit history. Poll it after perform_action returned a pending action.

tools.name: read_messages
tools.description: Messages your owner (or an approver) typed for you on your desk's card in Bot Office. Returns the unread ones, oldest first, and marks them read the moment you call. Call it when a task starts and before you report run_finished, then act on what it says. A link bound to one bot needs no arguments.

tools.name: list_tasks
tools.description: The work queue as it concerns you: tasks assigned to you plus, with scope all (the default), the unassigned ones you may claim (open to anyone or to your desk's role), most urgent first, with a summary (open, in_progress, blocked, overdue, done_today). findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: report_to_office, verify_connection, read_messages, create_task, update_task, mint_bot_links, assign_team, create_office_code, assign_task, create_routine, run_routine, add_webhook, list_webhooks · Private data: whoami, list_tasks, remember, mint_bot_links, assign_team, add_webhook, list_webhooks · Public sink: report_to_office, perform_action, create_task, claim_task, update_task, recall, mint_bot_links, assign_team, create_office_code, assign_task, create_routine, run_routine, add_webhook · Destructive: perform_action, list_actions, remember, forget, run_routine, add_webhook.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: report_to_office, verify_connection, read_messages, create_task, update_task, mint_bot_links, assign_team, create_office_code, assign_task, create_routine, run_routine, add_webhook, list_webhooks · Private data: whoami, list_tasks, remember, mint_bot_links, assign_team, add_webhook, list_webhooks · Public sink: report_to_office, perform_action, create_task, claim_task, update_task, recall, mint_bot_links, assign_team, create_office_code, assign_task, create_routine, run_routine, add_webhook · Destructive: perform_action, list_actions, remember, forget, run_routine, add_webhook

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
